classification.difficultyReason: Infer square-base dimensions and slant heights from two grid nets, then use Pythagoras and the pyramid volume formula.

content.prompt: The $6\times6$ grid below comprises squares of unit length. Each of the red regions can be folded into a square-based pyramid. Find their volumes.

spec.description: Six-by-six unit grid with the eight-vertex red net. Native TikZ is required because a blank-grid template cannot express the polygonal folding region. Grid lines remain visible through the light red fill.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied net and grid are visible; inferred dimensions and folding lines are absent.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{4\sqrt3}{3}$ cubic units.

Use the net to find the slant height, then use Pythagoras to find the perpendicular height.
answer.worked:
The central square has side length $2$, and each triangular face has slant height $2$. Let $h$ be the perpendicular height.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=2^2-1^2\\h&=\sqrt3\\V&=\frac13Ah\\V&=\frac13(2^2)(\sqrt3)\\V&=\frac{4\sqrt3}{3}\text{ cubic units}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Six-by-six unit grid with the eight-vertex red net. Native TikZ is required because a blank-grid template cannot express the polygonal folding region. Preserve the inward junctions and visible grid; do not add inferred folds.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied net and grid are visible; the inferred central square and calculated lengths are absent.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{8\sqrt6}{3}$ cubic units.

The base has diagonals $4$ and $4$; find the slant and perpendicular heights using Pythagoras.
answer.worked:
The square base joins the four inward corners and has diagonals $4$ and $4$. Its side length is $s$. A triangular face has slant height $l$, measured from an outer corner to the midpoint of its base edge.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(4)(4)\\A&=8\\s^2&=2^2+2^2\\s&=2\sqrt2\\l^2&=2^2+2^2\\l&=2\sqrt2\\h^2&=(2\sqrt2)^2-(\sqrt2)^2\\h&=\sqrt6\\V&=\frac13(8)(\sqrt6)\\V&=\frac{8\sqrt6}{3}\text{ cubic units}.\end{align*}$$
